Oral Communication on Closed Session Items Only
Closed Session
Reconvene to Regular Session / Roll Call / Report Out on Closed Session
Welcome by the School Board President, Mike Wells
Changes to the Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Oral Communication

publicComments.name: Azil
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student at Orion Mandarin Immersion advocated for an advanced ELA class at Kennedy Middle School, noting that English is her third language and advanced coursework would help her pursue her dream of becoming a pilot.

publicComments.name: Nia Seeberger
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student originally from China argued that students without English-speaking parents or outside resources especially need advanced ELA coursework at Kennedy to be prepared for AP classes in high school.

publicComments.name: Maple
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student scoring at the 92nd percentile nationally for 8th-grade ELA described feeling bored and disengaged in her current class and asked the board to add advanced ELA at Kennedy so she does not have to consider private school.

publicComments.name: Maya Rose Felix
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade student with parents who could not assist with homework asked the board to add advanced English at Kennedy, saying it is critical to her goal of becoming a lawyer and succeeding in AP coursework in high school.

publicComments.name: Greta
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student who chose Kennedy over North Star to continue Mandarin study asked the board to add advanced English and other challenging classes at Kennedy, noting she loses focus when material is too slow.

publicComments.name: Luis Velazquez
publicComments.summary: A parent and executive coach argued that eliminating advanced ELA in the name of equity is regressive, limiting students' potential, and urged the board to reinstate Advanced ELA at Kennedy for all students who want the challenge.

publicComments.name: Alexis Velazquez
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student whose iReady scores indicate readiness for 8th-grade instruction asked the board to add as many advanced classes as possible at Kennedy, open to any student who feels up for the challenge.

publicComments.name: Olbia
publicComments.summary: A fifth-grade Orion student planning to attend Kennedy asked the board to reinstate Advanced ELA, drawing a parallel to the existing advanced math program and arguing students with a high appetite for challenge should be grouped together.

publicComments.name: Megan
publicComments.summary: A community member supported the students' request for advanced coursework at Kennedy, arguing that limiting high achievers is ethically dubious, exacerbates achievement gaps, and that the district already has the staff and resources to expand advanced ELA across more school sites.

items.title: Bond Program Consent Items (Phase 2 Solar Change Orders #1 and #2 with Holt Renewables)
Bond Program Action Items
McKinley School Presentation for the 2024-2025 School Year
Discussion Items
Consent Items (MOU – SCCOE; Agreement – SMCOE; Chromebook Purchase)
Approval of Agreement with TeamCivX, Godbe Research, and SCI Consulting Group to Conduct a Parcel Tax Measure Feasibility Study

publicComments.name: Jessica Shade
publicComments.summary: A parent and parcel tax initiative leader expressed support for the feasibility study, saying the community group is willing to work with the district on either a citizen-led or district-led parcel tax initiative to fund teacher retention, STEAM programs, and smaller class sizes.

publicComments.name: Carlo Contavalli
publicComments.summary: A parent involved in the parcel tax initiative urged the board to move forward with the poll quickly, arguing that more funding is urgently needed to restore cut programs and support teachers.
